nodes.name: La Paz
nodes.why: Bolivia link: Avianca nonstop from Bogota

profile.tagline: Mountain-ringed highland capital with cable cars
profile.summary: Seat of government at about 3,600 m (El Alto airport at 4,000 m), spread down a canyon under Illimani. Loud, steep, chaotic and fascinating, with the best markets and the most tours in Bolivia.
things_to_do: Valle de la Luna and Chacaltaya day trips

hostels.name: Casa de huéspedes La Casa Bonita

profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. City dorm range USD 6-14 (bushop 2026).

nodes.name: Copacabana (Lake Titicaca)
nodes.why: Lakeside pilgrimage town, base for Isla del Sol and the Peru border (Kasani/Yunguyo)

profile.tagline: Lakeside pilgrim town on Titicaca
profile.summary: Small town at about 3,840 m on Lake Titicaca with a 17th-century basilica and the boats to Isla del Sol. Relaxed and backpacker-friendly, with trout on every menu; the Candelaria feast on 2 Feb brings dances and crowds.
things_to_do: Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana
Grilled lake trout on the waterfront
Pedal boat or kayak on the lake
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Isla del Sol
nodes.why: Titicaca island with Inca sites and a north-south hike; boats from Copacabana

profile.tagline: Car-free Inca island on Lake Titicaca
profile.summary: Rocky island with about 800 families, over 80 ruins, terraced hills and no cars or paved roads. Quiet village stays with big lake views; the north-south ridge walk is the draw.
things_to_do: Titi Qala sacred rock and Chinkana ruins
Sunrise and sunset from a Yumani guesthouse
Boat out to Isla de la Luna
profile.hostel_price_note: Guesthouses USD 15-50 per night (bushop 2026). Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Coroico (Yungas)
nodes.why: Subtropical Yungas town; La Paz-Coroico is usually done as a day trip or short stay (bushop)

image.credit: Phil Whitehouse from London, United Kingdom

profile.tagline: Warm green Yungas hill town above the jungle
profile.summary: Small town at about 1,500 m, much warmer than La Paz, with fruit, coca and cloud-forest views. Slow, hammock-and-pool pace, mostly weekend visitors from La Paz.
things_to_do: Death Road finish and Yungas road views
Pool and hammock day at a hillside hostel
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Oruro
nodes.why: Carnival city and rail/bus junction between La Paz, Uyuni and Cochabamba (Sajama NP base)

profile.tagline: Mining city and Carnaval capital, mostly a stopover
profile.summary: Cold high-plains city at about 3,700 m that wakes up for the Carnaval de Oruro in February (UNESCO listed). The rest of the year it is a quiet transit point with few travellers.
things_to_do: Virgen del Socavon sanctuary and mirador
profile.hostel_price_note: Very few hostels; accommodation fills and prices jump around Carnaval. Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Uyuni (Salar de Uyuni)
nodes.why: Gateway to the world's largest salt flat; mirror effect forms Dec-Mar; Incahuasi usually closed Jan-Mar

image.credit: Martin St-Amant (S23678); derivative work (noise reduction to sky) by Julia W

profile.tagline: Gateway to the world's biggest salt flat
profile.summary: Dusty railway town at 3,650 m that exists to launch Salar de Uyuni tours. Dec to Feb is rainy season, when a thin water layer gives the famous mirror effect but roads and tours can be disrupted.
things_to_do: Salar de Uyuni 1-day or 3-day jeep tour
Mirror effect at sunrise and sunset in rainy season
Lagunas Colorada and Verde on multi-day tours
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Tourist sources quote dorm USD 10-18 in Uyuni (touristsecrets 2026).

nodes.name: Potosi
nodes.why: 4,000 m UNESCO silver-mining city (Cerro Rico tours); on the Sucre-Uyuni-La Paz corridor

profile.tagline: Silver-mining city under Cerro Rico at 4,000 m
profile.summary: One of the world's highest cities, built on the silver of Cerro Rico. Cold, atmospheric colonial centre with working-miner history; mine tours are the draw and are not for everyone.
things_to_do: Casa Nacional de Moneda mint museum
Santa Teresa convent and cathedral tower
Colonial streets around Plaza 10 de Noviembre
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Sucre
nodes.why: Constitutional capital, white colonial city, mild climate; Tarabuco and dinosaur footprints nearby

profile.tagline: White colonial capital with a mild climate
profile.summary: Constitutional capital at 2,800 m with whitewashed colonial buildings, good cafes and a student feel. Milder and calmer than La Paz; popular for Spanish classes and long stays.
things_to_do: Plaza 25 de Mayo and Casa de la Libertad
Mirador de la Recoleta at sunset
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. City dorm range USD 6-14 (bushop 2026).

nodes.name: Tupiza
nodes.why: Red-canyon town in the south, starting point for Uyuni 4x4 tours and Villazon (Argentina) border

profile.tagline: Red-rock cowboy town in the far south
profile.summary: High-desert town at about 2,850 m among red canyons and cacti, tied to the Butch Cassidy legend. Quiet and frontier-like, the cheaper and calmer start for a 3-4 day Salar tour.
things_to_do: Horseback ride through Quebrada Palala and Valle de los Machos
Canyon del Inca and Puerta del Diablo
Butch Cassidy trail and San Vicente
4x4 start of the Salar de Uyuni tour (3 to 4 days)
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Cochabamba
nodes.why: Third-largest city, food capital, Cristo de la Concordia; road/air hub between altiplano and lowlands

profile.tagline: Local-feeling valley city known for food
profile.summary: Warm valley city at 2,550 m with a mild climate and Bolivia's best eating scene. Few tourists, big markets and a laid-back university-town pace.
things_to_do: Cristo de la Concordia hilltop statue
Lunch at a picanteria (silpancho, pique macho)
Day trip to Tarata or Incallajta ruins
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Santa Cruz de la Sierra
nodes.why: Bolivia link: Avianca nonstop from Bogota, Copa from Panama

profile.tagline: Fast-growing lowland business city
profile.summary: Hot, flat and modern, Bolivia's biggest city and a trade hub. Mostly a practical stop with a pleasant colonial plaza, good restaurants and the base for Samaipata and the Jesuit missions.
things_to_do: Plaza 24 de Septiembre and the cathedral tower
Biocentro Guembe butterfly and orchid park
Lowland cooking and cafes around Equipetrol
Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos day tour
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Samaipata
nodes.why: Cool hill-town with El Fuerte (UNESCO) and Amboro NP; weekend retreat from Santa Cruz

profile.tagline: Laid-back expat and backpacker valley town
profile.summary: Small town at about 1,650 m in the foothills near Amboro park with a big foreign-resident scene. Cafes, hammocks and cloud-forest walks, and the base for the pre-Inca El Fuerte site.
things_to_do: El Fuerte de Samaipata carved rock ruins (UNESCO)
Amboro National Park waterfalls and tree ferns
Cafe and bakery lunches on the plaza
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. One source quoted Hostel Serena dorms from GBP 9.5 and privates from GBP 29 (alongdustyroads, 2025); not converted to DKK.

nodes.name: Rurrenabaque (Madidi)
nodes.why: Amazon-edge jungle and pampas tour base for Madidi NP; flights and roads disrupted in rainy season (peak Jan-Feb)

profile.tagline: Amazon gateway on the Beni River
profile.summary: Hot, humid river town where the Andes drop into the lowlands. Gateway for Madidi jungle lodges and the Pampas wildlife tours; Dec to Feb is rainy season so trails and flights can be disrupted.
things_to_do: Madidi National Park jungle lodge stay
Pampas boat tour with caiman, capybara and pink dolphins
Beni River sunset and the ferry to San Buenaventura
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Puno (Peru, reference)
nodes.why: Peruvian Titicaca port and transfer point for Copacabana; nearest airport Juliaca (JUL) about 1 h

nodes.name: Cusco (Peru, reference)
nodes.why: Machu Picchu gateway; tourist bus to La Paz (12-14 h) and Avianca flight CUZ-LPB

nodes.name: Lima (Peru, reference)
nodes.why: Peru's hub; direct flights to La Paz and Santa Cruz (BoA, LATAM)

nodes.name: Bogota
nodes.why: Capital and main air hub; flights to every Colombian node plus Panama, Central America and Bolivia

image.credit: Panorama_van_bogota.jpg: Jan Arkesteijn derivative work: Niclond23 (talk)

profile.tagline: Cool, high-altitude capital with a graffiti-covered old town
profile.summary: Colombia's 2,640 m capital is a sprawling city of museums, street art and food, and Dec to Jan are its driest, sunniest months. Expect cool nights (6 to 8 C) and an urban, big-city pace rather than a beach vibe.
things_to_do: La Candelaria old town and street art

nodes.name: Panama City
nodes.why: Copa hub; nearest big neighbour region to Colombia by air

profile.tagline: Skyline capital with a colonial old quarter and the Canal
profile.summary: Panama City mixes a glass skyline, the Panama Canal and the restored Casco Viejo old quarter with rooftop bars. The main arrival hub in the region and base for the San Blas and Colombia routes.
things_to_do: Miraflores Locks on the Panama Canal
Cinta Costera and Mercado de Mariscos

nodes.name: San Jose (Costa Rica)
nodes.why: Central America link from Bogota and Cartagena (Avianca Costa Rica, Copa)

image.credit: Costa Rica - San Jose and National Museum (5378828668).jpg: Andy Rusch from Santa Barbara, USA derivative work: ויקיג'אנ

profile.tagline: Costa Rican capital, mainly a hub
profile.summary: San Jose is a busy highland capital with a handful of museums and markets, mostly used as a hub for buses and flights. Not a highlight in itself, but it has a decent hostel scene.
things_to_do: Day trip to Poas or Irazu volcano

nodes.name: Guatemala City
nodes.why: Capital, La Aurora airport and the hub for buses to Flores, Lanquin, El Salvador and Honduras

profile.tagline: Big, loud capital that most travellers only pass through
profile.summary: Guatemala City is the country's sprawling capital and the hub for onward buses, with a historic centre (Zona 1) and a modern Zona 10 and Zona 4. The vibe is busy and urban, with most backpackers staying one night before heading to Antigua, Flores or the border.
things_to_do: Palacio Nacional and Plaza de la Constitucion in Zona 1
Museo Popol Vuh and Museo Ixchel
Day trip to Antigua or Pacaya

nodes.name: Guadalajara
nodes.why: Jalisco capital and Mexico's second-largest hub; base for Tequila, Chapala, Guanajuato, Vallarta

profile.tagline: Mexico's mariachi and tequila capital
profile.summary: Large, walkable-in-parts city with a grand colonial centre, big food and craft-market culture and a lively student and art scene. Dec to Feb is dry and sunny.
things_to_do: Centro Historico: cathedral, Plaza de Armas, Hospicio Cabanas
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

nodes.name: Tequila
nodes.why: Agave landscape UNESCO town; tequila distillery tours; day trip from Guadalajara

profile.tagline: Agave landscape town and tequila heartland
profile.summary: UNESCO-listed agave landscape an hour from Guadalajara, built around distilleries. Pretty plaza and tasting rooms; most visitors come as a day trip.
things_to_do: Tequila Express or Jose Cuervo Express train
Plaza and parish of Santiago Apostol
profile.hostel_price_note: No hostels found; most visitors day-trip from Guadalajara. Prices null.

nodes.name: Guanajuato
nodes.why: Colorful UNESCO colonial city (Bajio airport BJX near Leon about 0.5 h); about 4 h from Guadalajara

profile.tagline: Colourful silver-mining university city
profile.summary: Steep hillside city of tunnels, plazas and pastel houses, UNESCO listed. Student energy, callejoneadas and museums in a small walkable centre.
things_to_do: Alley of the Kiss and Teatro Juarez
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Hostelz Mexico average: no figure for Guanajuato.

nodes.name: Lake Chapala / Ajijic
nodes.why: Lake Chapala and expat town Ajijic; day trip from Guadalajara by Chapala Plus bus

profile.tagline: Lakeside retiree and artist villages
profile.summary: Mexico's biggest lake, with Chapala town and Ajijic's cobbled artsy village, a large North American expat community. Very calm; the lake is not a swimming draw.
things_to_do: Scorpion Island and Mezcala boat trip
profile.hostel_price_note: Only one hostel listed (dorm 'from MX$83' on Hostelz, not converted). Hotels and Airbnbs dominate.

nodes.name: Puerto Vallarta
nodes.why: Pacific resort and beach hub; flights and ETN/Primera Plus buses from Guadalajara

profile.tagline: Pacific resort town with cobbled old centre
profile.summary: Beach and party town on Banderas Bay with a malecon, Zona Romantica and jungle-backed beaches. Dec to Feb is peak season with humpback whales and high prices.
things_to_do: Zona Romantica and Playa Los Muertos
profile.hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Peak season dorm prices run above the average.

nodes.name: Antigua Guatemala
nodes.why: Colonial town and the main backpacker base with the densest shuttle network in Guatemala

image.credit: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

profile.tagline: Colonial town under three volcanoes
profile.summary: Antigua is a cobbled UNESCO colonial town and the main backpacker base in Guatemala, ringed by Agua, Fuego and Acatenango volcanoes. Compact, walkable and very touristy, with language students, cafes, rooftop bars and a dense shuttle network.
things_to_do: Arch of Santa Catalina and Parque Central
Colonial ruins (Capuchinas, San Francisco el Grande)

nodes.name: Lake Atitlan (Panajachel / San Pedro)
nodes.why: Volcano lake with Panajachel gateway and San Pedro / San Marcos / San Juan villages reached by lancha

profile.tagline: Volcano lake of Maya villages, better for relaxing than partying
profile.summary: Lake Atitlan is a deep volcanic lake ringed by villages, each with its own character: Panajachel is the gateway, San Pedro is the backpacker and party base, San Marcos and Santa Cruz are yoga and chill spots. Boats (lanchas) link everything, and the pace is slow.
things_to_do: Climb San Pedro or Atitlan volcano
Kayak or dive from Santa Cruz La Laguna
Visit Santiago Atitlan and the Maximon shrine

nodes.name: Quetzaltenango (Xela)
nodes.why: Highland city, Spanish schools, volcano hikes, route to Mexico border

profile.tagline: Highland university city with Spanish schools and volcano hikes
profile.summary: Quetzaltenango (Xela) is Guatemala's second city, a working highland town with far fewer tourists than Antigua. The vibe is local and student-driven, with cheap Spanish schools, hot springs and a base for volcano treks.

nodes.name: Flores / Tikal
nodes.why: Island town at Lake Peten Itza, gateway to Tikal and the Belize border (San Ignacio)

image.credit: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

profile.tagline: Lake-island town and gateway to Tikal
profile.summary: Flores is a small, colourful island in Lake Peten Itza linked by a causeway, and the base for Tikal, the Belize border and long bus legs. Relaxed and walkable, with lakeside bars and sunsets, and many people leave at 4am for Tikal sunrise.
things_to_do: Tikal ruins at sunrise or sunset
Swim and sunset at the lake
Cave and cenote day trips (Actun Kan)
Walk the island and its lakefront bars

nodes.name: Lanquin / Semuc Champey
nodes.why: Turquoise pools and caves in Alta Verapaz, backpacker staple

profile.tagline: Jungle river hostels at the gate of Semuc Champey
profile.summary: Lanquin is a small village in the Alta Verapaz hills and the base for Semuc Champey's turquoise limestone pools. Hostels sit along the river in the jungle, with a social, party-leaning backpacker crowd and rough minibus access.
things_to_do: Swim the Semuc Champey pools and walk to the mirador
Hostel river swings and communal dinners

nodes.name: San Salvador
nodes.why: Central America link from Bogota (Avianca nonstop)

profile.tagline: Buzzing Central American capital with a growing food and museum scene
profile.summary: San Salvador is a bustling, polarised capital of malls, nightlife and gritty districts, ringed by volcanoes. Most travellers use it as a hub and spend a day or two on museums, pupusas and viewpoints before heading to the coast.
things_to_do: Los Planes de Renderos viewpoint and pupusas

hostels.name: Hostal Cumbres del Volcan Flor Blanca

nodes.name: El Tunco / El Zonte coast
nodes.why: Surf and backpacker beach town on the Pacific coast, about 1 h from SAL airport

profile.tagline: Small surf village with sunset rock and weekend parties
profile.summary: El Tunco is a tiny black-sand surf village on El Salvador's Pacific coast, busy with backpackers and Salvadoran weekenders. El Zonte, a few km along the coast, is the quieter surf and Bitcoin-beach alternative.
things_to_do: Learn to surf at El Sunzal, La Bocana or Bocanita
Weekend live music and bar crawl

hostels.name: The Salty Dogs Hostel - El Tunco

nodes.name: Copan Ruinas
nodes.why: Maya ruins town just over the Guatemala border at El Florido; shuttle crossing point

profile.tagline: Calm Maya-ruins town with a famous hieroglyphic stairway
profile.summary: Copan Ruinas is a small, relaxed Honduran hill town of cobbled, colourful streets beside one of the best Maya sites in the region. Easy walking, coffee, birds and hot springs, with a mellow backpacker crowd.
things_to_do: Copan archaeological park and Hieroglyphic Stairway
Tea and chocolate tasting in town

nodes.name: San Pedro Sula
nodes.why: Honduras' commercial hub and international airport; bus gateway to La Ceiba and Tegucigalpa

profile.tagline: Industrial Honduran hub, a transit stop
profile.summary: San Pedro Sula is Honduras' commercial centre and the main bus and air hub for the north coast and Copan. It is a working city with little for visitors beyond onward connections.

nodes.name: Tegucigalpa
nodes.why: Honduran capital, on the Tica Bus / Pullmantur line between San Salvador and Managua

profile.tagline: Hilly colonial capital, mostly a transit point
profile.summary: Tegucigalpa is a sprawling hillside capital with a small colonial core, steep stone streets and big city views. Few travellers stay long, but it is the link for Nicaragua and the south.
things_to_do: Catedral de San Miguel Arcangel and Parque Central

nodes.name: La Ceiba
nodes.why: North coast port town; ferry terminals to Roatan and Utila, Pico Bonito, rafting

profile.tagline: Caribbean port city and ferry gateway to the Bay Islands
profile.summary: La Ceiba is a friendly, laid-back Caribbean port city and the departure point for ferries to Roatan and Utila. It also works as a base for rafting and national parks.
things_to_do: White-water rafting on the Cangrejal river

nodes.name: Roatan
nodes.why: Largest Bay Island: West End and West Bay, diving and beaches

profile.tagline: Largest Bay Island, diving and beaches at higher prices
profile.summary: Roatan is the biggest of Honduras' Bay Islands, with diving, snorkelling and white-sand beaches, plus cruise-ship traffic at the resort end. West End is the backpacker base and West Bay the best beach, and it is pricier than the mainland.
things_to_do: Roatan Brewing Co. and rum tasting

nodes.name: Utila
nodes.why: Cheapest diving in the Caribbean, backpacker island with no scheduled flights

profile.tagline: Backpacker dive island with cheap certification
profile.summary: Utila is the smallest and cheapest of the Bay Islands, a low-key Caribbean dive island with a social backpacker scene. Most people come to learn to dive and stay longer than planned.
things_to_do: Snorkel and swim at Chepes Beach

nodes.name: Managua
nodes.why: Capital and hub for all Nicaraguan buses, shuttles and the Corn Islands flights

image.credit: Department of Commerce. Bureau of Public Roads. 8/20/1949-4/1/1967

profile.tagline: Sprawling lakeside capital, mainly a transit stop
profile.summary: Managua is Nicaragua's spread-out capital on Lake Managua, without a real centre, and most travellers move straight on to Granada or Leon. Hot, busy and car-oriented.
things_to_do: Old cathedral ruins and Plaza de la Revolucion
Onward day trip to Masaya volcano

nodes.name: Leon
nodes.why: Colonial university city, volcano boarding, Pacific beaches

image.credit: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

profile.tagline: Revolutionary university city and volcano-boarding base
profile.summary: Leon is a hot, intellectual colonial city of grand churches, murals and student bars. A popular backpacker stop with cheap beds, and it is where people go to board down Cerro Negro.
things_to_do: Rooftop of the Cathedral of Leon
Day trip to Las Penitas beach

nodes.name: Granada
nodes.why: Colonial city on Lake Nicaragua; base for Masaya, Mombacho and Ometepe

profile.tagline: Colourful colonial city on Lake Nicaragua
profile.summary: Granada is Nicaragua's pastel colonial showpiece beside Lake Nicaragua, with a lively pedestrian street, plazas and many hostels. Tourist-oriented but relaxed, and the base for Masaya and Mombacho.
things_to_do: Calle La Calzada bars and restaurants
Isletas boat trip on Lake Nicaragua
Climb the Cathedral or La Merced tower

nodes.name: San Juan del Sur
nodes.why: Surf and party beach town, 30 km from the Costa Rica border

image.credit: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

profile.tagline: Pacific surf town and Sunday Funday party hub
profile.summary: San Juan del Sur is a beach town in a horseshoe bay, with surf camps, sunset hill views and a big party scene. The most tourist-focused place in Nicaragua, with a large expat crowd.
things_to_do: Surf lessons at Playa Maderas or Hermosa

nodes.name: Ometepe
nodes.why: Twin-volcano island in Lake Nicaragua, ferry from San Jorge to Moyogalpa

image.credit: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

profile.tagline: Twin-volcano island in Lake Nicaragua with slow rural life
profile.summary: Ometepe is a figure-eight island formed by Concepcion and Maderas volcanoes in Lake Nicaragua. Farms, jungle lodges and beaches give it a slow, outdoorsy vibe, and travel across it is by bus or scooter.
things_to_do: Kayak or SUP at Charco Verde

nodes.name: Big Corn Island
nodes.why: Caribbean island with La Costena flights from MGA; gateway to Little Corn

profile.tagline: Quiet Caribbean island with Creole culture
profile.summary: Big Corn Island is the larger and more developed of the two Corn Islands, quiet, English-Creole in character and good for relaxing, snorkelling and sunsets. It is the arrival point by plane or panga from the mainland.

nodes.name: Little Corn Island
nodes.why: Car-free Caribbean island reached by panga from Big Corn

profile.tagline: Car-free barefoot Caribbean island
profile.summary: Little Corn is a one-square-mile island with no cars, sandy paths, simple lodges and a small but lively social scene. Remote and basic, with limited hot water and electricity.
things_to_do: Yoga at Firefly or the Lighthouse

nodes.name: Liberia (Costa Rica)
nodes.why: Northwest Costa Rica airport and bus hub, 3 h from San Juan del Sur by shuttle

profile.tagline: Dry-forest gateway city to Guanacaste beaches and the Nicaragua border
profile.summary: Liberia is a hot, practical town in Guanacaste with an international airport, used as a base for beaches, volcano parks and the Penas Blancas crossing. Quiet, with a few hostels.
things_to_do: Rincon de la Vieja national park
Day trip to Santa Rosa national park

nodes.name: San Blas / Guna Yala
nodes.why: Guna Yala island chain; the standard Panama to Colombia sailing or speedboat route

profile.tagline: Guna-run island archipelago of white-sand cays
profile.summary: San Blas (Guna Yala) is an autonomous Guna territory of about 365 small islands on Panama's Caribbean coast. Stays are basic cabins or sailing trips, with no ATMs, and Guna culture and molas are central.
things_to_do: Visit a Guna community and buy molas

nodes.name: Capurgana
nodes.why: Car-free Caribbean beach town near the Panama border (airstrip CPB charters)

profile.tagline: Roadless Caribbean village on the Colombia-Panama border
profile.summary: Capurgana is a small, car-free village in Choco reached only by boat or plane, with jungle trails and calm bays, and the usual stepping stone for Darien crossings. Quiet and low-key.
things_to_do: Walk the jungle trails to El Cielito waterfall
Snorkel at La Mocha and Playa Aguacate
Boat or walk to Sapzurro and La Miel

nodes.name: Medellin
nodes.why: Most popular backpacker city; second air hub (JMC airport 45 min out, Olaya Herrera EOH for Clic/Satena)

profile.tagline: City of eternal spring with a reinvented, creative core
profile.summary: Warm valley city (about 22 C all year) known for its metro cable cars, Botero sculptures and a big backpacker and nomad scene around El Poblado. Dec brings the Alumbrados Christmas lights across the city.
things_to_do: Botero Plaza and Museum of Antioquia

nodes.name: Cali
nodes.why: Salsa capital in the south; air link to Caribbean coast and San Andres

profile.tagline: Salsa capital of the world, hot and unpolished
profile.summary: Large, hot valley city (about 1,000 m, 24 C average) where salsa clubs and dance schools are the main draw, with far fewer foreign tourists than Medellin or Cartagena. The Cali Fair runs 25 to 30 Dec with concerts and salsa shows.
things_to_do: Cerro de las Tres Cruces hike

nodes.name: Cartagena
nodes.why: Walled colonial city, top Caribbean destination and Panama flight/boat gateway

profile.tagline: Walled UNESCO colonial city on the Caribbean
profile.summary: Pastel colonial streets inside 16th century walls, a hip Getsemani quarter and boat trips to the Rosario Islands; very hot and humid but Dec to Apr is the dry season. The most touristy stop in the country, with prices to match.
things_to_do: Walled City walk and Plaza de Bolivar

hostels.name: Republica Hostel Cartagena
hostels.note: Dorm 'from' rate in $ (currency not stated, treated as USD); article written 2019, page modified Aug 2026

profile.notes: Hostelz Getsemani page lists dorm beds from about $4 across the district; prices above are older and likely low.

nodes.name: Santa Marta
nodes.why: Gateway to Tayrona, Minca, Palomino and the Sierra Nevada

image.credit: Alejandro Bayer Tamayo from Armenia, Colombia

profile.tagline: Caribbean port town and gateway to Tayrona, Minca and Palomino
profile.summary: Colombia's oldest surviving city is a hot, gritty bay town best used as a base for the Sierra Nevada coast. Dry season runs Dec to Apr, so beach and trekking weather is good.

nodes.name: Pereira
nodes.why: Coffee region air and bus hub for Salento, Manizales and Cocora

profile.tagline: Coffee Axis transport hub with an airport
profile.summary: Largest city in the coffee region and the usual gateway to Salento, Manizales and Armenia, with a busy bus terminal and Matecana airport. Little reason to stay beyond a night, though the Megacable gondola and Lake Otun are options.
things_to_do: Gateway to Salento and Cocora Valley (about 45 min)

nodes.name: San Andres
nodes.why: Caribbean island, direct flights from most Colombian cities and Panama

profile.tagline: Caribbean island of seven shades of blue, far off the mainland
profile.summary: Duty-free island 700 km from the mainland with a crowded main beach strip, reef snorkelling and golf-cart touring; English-based Creole culture gives it a different feel from the rest of Colombia. Busy at New Year and on weekends, quieter in the villages like San Luis.

nodes.name: Providencia
nodes.why: Quiet island reached only by Satena flight or ferry from San Andres

profile.tagline: Quiet, hilly Creole island for diving and slow days
profile.summary: About 5,000 residents, English-Creole speaking, with a Rastafari and Raizal heritage, and a UNESCO Seaflower reserve around it. Rebuilt after Hurricane Iota (2020), mostly small guesthouses and cabanas.
things_to_do: Scuba and snorkelling in Seaflower reserve
profile.notes: Hostel prices not found in allowed sources; hotel/guesthouse names are from a 2012 article, verify they survived Hurricane Iota (2020).

nodes.name: Salento (Valle de Cocora)
nodes.why: Coffee-region village and gateway to Valle de Cocora wax palms

profile.tagline: Colourful coffee-region village at the gate of Cocora Valley
profile.summary: A pretty bahareque village of balconies and craft shops, famous for the 60 m wax palms of the Cocora Valley a jeep ride away. Packed at weekends and holidays, calm mid-week.
things_to_do: Valle de Cocora wax palm hike
Coffee farm tour (e.g. Don Elias, Finca el Ocaso)
Trout and patacon on the plaza

nodes.name: Manizales
nodes.why: Coffee-region city near Los Nevados; La Nubia airport has Clic flights

profile.tagline: High-altitude coffee city and university town under a volcano
profile.summary: Steep, cool, spring-like city at about 2,150 m with 30,000 students and the closest base for Nevado del Ruiz and hot springs. Far fewer foreign tourists than Salento. Not usually on the gringo trail.

nodes.name: Guatape
nodes.why: Lake town and El Penol rock, standard Medellin day trip (about 2 h)

profile.tagline: Painted lakeside town below El Penol rock
profile.summary: Technicolour zocalo-tiled houses on a man-made reservoir, 2 hours from Medellin and swamped by day-trippers at weekends. Staying overnight gives you the calm evenings and quiet mornings.
things_to_do: Zocalo streets and Plaza de Zocalos
Kayak or paddleboard on the lake

nodes.name: Tayrona National Park
nodes.why: Top Caribbean beach park, entrances El Zaino, Calabazo, Palangana, Bahia Concha

profile.tagline: Jungle-and-beach national park on the Caribbean coast
profile.summary: Coastal rainforest park with white beaches reached on foot or horse, hammock camping at Cabo San Juan and strong currents on most beaches. Typically closes about 1 to 15 February for indigenous rest, so check dates against your itinerary.
things_to_do: Hike to Cabo San Juan beach
Hammock night at Cabo San Juan

nodes.name: Palomino
nodes.why: Backpacker beach town with river tubing, on the coast road east of Tayrona

profile.tagline: Barefoot beach village where the river meets the sea
profile.summary: Laid-back strip of hostels, hammocks and dirt roads between the Sierra Nevada and the Caribbean, with a wide windy beach and river tubing. Backpacker-friendly and growing quickly.

nodes.name: Minca
nodes.why: Cloud-forest village above Santa Marta, hostels and coffee farms

profile.tagline: Cool mountain hamlet above Santa Marta with jungle ecolodges
profile.summary: Small Sierra Nevada village at about 600 m, popular for waterfalls, coffee farms, birdwatching and sunset viewpoints, and 20 degrees cooler than the coast at night. Most travellers stay in ecolodges outside the village.

nodes.name: Barranquilla
nodes.why: Transfer city between Cartagena and Santa Marta, airport with Avianca/LATAM/Wingo/JetSmart

profile.tagline: Hot industrial port city, home of Colombia's biggest Carnival
profile.summary: Fourth biggest city (1.3 million), relaxed Caribbean pace, Art Deco and Magdalena riverfront; mostly a transit stop but the Carnival is a big draw. Carnival 2027 is expected around 6 to 9 Feb (Saturday to Tuesday before Ash Wednesday, 10 Feb), confirm locally.
profile.notes: Carnival date is derived from Ash Wednesday 10 Feb 2027, not from a source.

nodes.name: San Gil (and Barichara)
nodes.why: Adventure sports capital of Santander, base for Barichara and Chicamocha

profile.tagline: Adventure capital of Colombia in the Santander hills
profile.summary: Small market town packed with outfitters for rafting, paragliding over Chicamocha canyon, canyoning and caving, with cheap hostels and a young crowd. Barichara, a preserved white colonial village, is 45 minutes away and quieter.
things_to_do: White water rafting on the Suarez or Fonce
Barichara and the Camino Real to Guane
profile.notes: Barichara (Hostelz, Oct 2026, USD): NOMAD Hostal dorm $12.06, Casa Nacuma dorm $12.41; Barichara city average private about $28 in Dec.

nodes.name: Villa de Leyva
nodes.why: Colonial town 3-4 h from Bogota

profile.tagline: Whitewashed colonial town with the largest plaza in Colombia
profile.summary: Cobbled streets, 16th century buildings and a 14,000 sqm plaza, three hours from Bogota and very busy at weekends and holidays. Dry desert-like valley with fossils, wineries and cloud forest nearby.
things_to_do: Pozos Azules and Iguaque National Park
profile.notes: Hostelz general estimate: dorm about $5, private about $12 (looks low).

nodes.name: Necocli
nodes.why: Gulf of Uraba port where boats leave for Capurgana (main route toward Panama)

profile.tagline: Gulf of Uraba port town where boats leave for Capurgana
profile.summary: Afro-Colombian beach town, mainly a staging point for boats to Capurgana and Acandi; hot and basic. Also used as a transit point for Darien migrants.
things_to_do: Boat launches to Capurgana and Acandi
profile.notes: Hostelz prices are listing 'from' rates, no date shown.

nodes.name: Sapzurro
nodes.why: Bay village 10-15 min by boat from Capurgana; trail up to the La Miel border post

profile.tagline: Tiny car-free bay village on the Panama border
profile.summary: About 270 residents on a sheltered bay, no roads and no ATMs, with jungle trails to Panama's La Miel beach. Reach by boat from Capurgana (COP 10,000 per sygic guide).
things_to_do: Walk to Playa Blanca and La Miel (Panama)
Hike over the hill to Capurgana (about 1.5 h)
Cabo Tiburon, border of South and Central America
profile.notes: No hostel prices found in allowed sources. Accommodation is cabanas, rooms, hammocks and camping. Bring cash, no ATMs.

nodes.name: Puerto Obaldia
nodes.why: Panamanian border town with immigration; Air Panama flights to Panama City

profile.tagline: Panamanian border post and airstrip on the Guna Yala coast
profile.summary: Remote settlement of about 670 people with customs and immigration, no roads, only boats and a small airstrip. A functional crossing, not a place to stay.
things_to_do: Boat to or from Sapzurro (about 45 min)
profile.notes: No hostel data found. Sygic guide quotes US$15 launch from Puerto Obaldia to Sapzurro.
